title: Casper and the Visitor
premise: Lior Eastwick, a meticulous pest controller in the dying town of Hollowmere, is called to a farmhouse where something leaves human fingerprints on the inside of sealed walls. The intruder is Wren, Lior's childhood imaginary friend, unchanged after twenty years — and Wren has been keeping the founders' half-finished ritual alive to stop the well beneath the town from refilling with everything it was fed. As Lior documents the impossible and the town's descendants close ranks around their inherited guilt, they must choose between loyalty to Wren and the truth of what the founders did. In the end, Lior completes the ritual not as an exorcism but as a testimony, reading the founders' crimes aloud into the well until it accepts the record instead of more bodies — and Wren, finally witnessed, dissolves into the clean water.
about_author: Mirabel Vane spent a decade as a municipal records clerk in rural England before turning to horror, and her fiction remains obsessed with ledgers, permits, and the terrible things filed neatly between lines. She writes from a converted tithe barn where she keeps, she insists, a complete inventory of every room.

chapters.title: Call-Out
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A routine job at the Harrow farm turns strange: scratching inside sealed plaster, then five small fingerprints pressed into fresh paint from within the wall. Lior photographs everything, logs times, treats documentation like prayer. Emotional beat: professional calm stretched thin over childhood dread.

chapters.title: The Porch
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At home that night, Wren is waiting on the porch — exactly as imagined at age seven, mud-stained and patient. Wren says only: 'You were supposed to help me finish it.' Lior records the conversation on their phone; the recording plays back as water sounds. Beat: wonder curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, interleaved with ledger excerpts. Researching Hollowmere's founding families, Lior finds gaps in the archives — pages razored out, wells omitted from surveys. The Harrows are founder-descendants. Beat: the thrill of investigation shadowed by the sense of being watched through the town itself.

chapters.title: What the Well Was Fed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, first time. Wren remembers being made — invented by a lonely child, then repurposed by the founders as a vessel to carry confessions down to the well so it would stay quiet. Wren has been holding the ritual's last line for twenty years, alone. Beat: grief for a friend who was never allowed to be just a friend.

chapters.title: Descendants
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior confronts Ada Harrow, who knows exactly what lives in her walls and pays quietly to keep it contained. Ada offers Lior money and a warning: the last person who tried to finish the ritual drowned in a dry well. Beat: temptation of complicity versus the itch of justice.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The well begins refilling early — livestock gone, taps running dark, children sleepwalking toward the town square. Wren weakens as the water rises, becoming translucent. Lior realizes the containment isn't maintenance; it's a countdown. Beat: dread accelerating into urgency.

chapters.title: The Missing Line
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses why the founders' ritual failed: the final line requires a willing witness who names the crime aloud — and every descendant chose silence. Wren asks Lior to be the witness, knowing what it will cost them both. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly between old friends.

chapters.title: Sealed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Ada and the other descendants trap Lior in the Harrow house, nailing shut the room with the fingerprints, deciding Lior is part of the infestation now. Inside the sealed room, Lior finds the founders' original rite scratched into the lath — and understands the well was never hungry; it was starved of acknowledgment. Beat: terror transmuting into clarity.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax. Alternating POVs at the wellhead at dawn. Lior breaks free with Wren's help and reads the founders' crimes aloud — names, dates, the children fed to the water — while the descendants scream and the well rises to take them. The well stills, listens, and begins to drain. Beat: justice outside the law, spoken rather than enforced.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, Hollowmere's water runs clear and cold. Lior files one final report — a full account of everything, addressed to no office that exists — and leaves it on the porch where Wren used to wait. The pages are damp in the morning, but the handwriting on the last line isn't Lior's. Beat: mourning braided with peace; loyalty outlasting truth.
